title: Sum of Prefix Scores of Words
hints: a prefix's count is exactly 'how many words pass through this point in a trie' - so build the trie once and get every prefix count as a byproduct of insertion
insert every word into the trie; at each node you pass through while inserting a word (including the final node), increment that node's pass-through counter by one
once all words are inserted, every node's counter equals the prefix count for the path from root to that node
for each word, walk the trie along its own characters again, and sum up the counters at every node visited - that sum is exactly its prefix score
commonMistakes: recomputing prefix counts with a fresh scan per word instead of reusing the shared trie counters, which defeats the point
forgetting to increment the counter at the ROOT's children on the very first character of each word (off-by-one in the insertion loop)
not handling duplicate words correctly, since they should still both contribute to and read from the same shared counters

content.problemStatement:
You're given a space-delimited string of lowercase words (the list may
contain duplicates). For a given prefix string p, define its "prefix
count" as the number of words in the whole list that start with p. For
each word in the list, define its "prefix score" as the sum of the
prefix counts of all of its own non-empty prefixes, from length 1 up to
its full length.

**Return the prefix score of every word, as a list in the same order as the input list.**
constraints: words consist only of lowercase English letters
notes: duplicate words in the list (both count toward each other's prefix counts)
a single-character word (score equals just its own prefix count)
words that share no prefixes with any other word (each prefix count is 1)

sampleTestCases.explanation: prefix counts: "a"=2, "ab"=2, "abc"=1, "b"=2, "bc"=1; "abc" scores a+ab+abc = 2+2+1 = 5; "ab" scores a+ab = 2+2 = 4; "bc" scores b+bc = 2+1 = 3; "b" scores b = 2
a single word: each of its 4 prefixes has count 1, sum = 4
each prefix ("w","wo","wow") has count 2 since both entries share them, so each word scores 2+2+2 = 6

optimal.time: O(total characters) to build and to answer all queries
optimal.pattern: insert every word into a trie, incrementing a counter at every node visited during each insertion; then for each word, walk the trie again and sum the counters along its path

bruteForce.approach: for each word, for each of its prefixes, scan the entire word list counting how many words start with that prefix, and sum those counts
bruteForce.time: O(n * m^2) where n is word count and m is max word length
